processing: A tea cultivar, not a finished style. In Yibin Early Tea it goes through spreading, fixing, shaping or rolling and drying into a flat green tea.
harvest_season: Used for Yibin Early Tea, a spring green tea; the cultivar's own budding dates are not well documented.
appearance_dry: In Yibin Early Tea, flat, straight strands of a glossy emerald green.
appearance_liquor: In Yibin Early Tea, a bright tender green.
appearance_wet: In Yibin Early Tea, tender, bright green leaf.
taste_profile: Nothing is well documented for the cultivar alone; Yibin Early Tea, which relies on it, has a chestnut aroma and a fresh, sweet, mellow taste.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a Sichuan spring green, since the cultivar is rarely sold under its own name.

vintage_note: Rarely if ever sold under the cultivar name. You meet it inside Yibin Early Tea, which as a green tea is sold as a current-year spring harvest and is best drunk fresh.
description:
Zaobaijian 5, also written Zaobaijian No. 5, is a tea cultivar linked to Yibin in southern Sichuan. It is one of the main varieties behind Yibin Early Tea, the area's protected green tea, along with Fuxuan 9.

This is a plant variety and not a recipe, so the leaf could in principle be made in different ways. The documented use is in Yibin Early Tea, which is spread, fixed, shaped and dried into flat, straight strands.

No reliable tasting notes exist for the cultivar on its own. The tea it goes into is described as chestnut-scented, fresh and sweet, and it brews like other Sichuan spring greens.

If you want to try it, look for Yibin Early Tea and ask the seller which variety was used, since most packs will not say.
history: Little is documented about who bred this cultivar or when. It is known mainly as a principal variety of Yibin Early Tea; details of its selection and any official registration are unclear.
